title: A boom town of thousands
text: By 1900, roughly 3,500 to 4,000 people lived in Randsburg. The town had a 30-stamp ore crusher, a bank, churches, and theaters. At the turn of the century, when gold was worth only 12 to 16 dollars an ounce, the Yellow Aster Mine recovered 3 million dollars in gold. Two fires within months of each other destroyed much of the town, and a third took out most of the remaining buildings.
